newsitem.title: JAPAN: KDD, Japan Telecom undecided on cell phone format.
newsitem.headline: KDD, Japan Telecom undecided on cell phone format.

text.p: Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd and Japan Telecom Co Ltd said on Monday they have not decided on the format for the CDMA cellular phone technology to be used in their next-generation cell phones.

Business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported in its evening edition on Monday that KDD and Japan Telecom would develop their next-generation cell phones under the format currently being developed by Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp's NTT Mobile Communications Network Inc (NTT DoCoMo).
"We have not decided whether to use the DoCoMo format, as an industry organisation is currently in the process of drawing up the standard in Japan," said a KDD spokesman.
A spokeswoman for Japan Telecom also said the company has not decided which format it will use.
The company officials said there is an ongoing tug-of-war in the Japanese phone industry between NTT DoCoMo's format and another CDMA format promoted by Motorola Inc of the United States.
DDI Corp announced earlier that it would adopt the Motorola format developed by Qualcomm Inc in the 1998/99 business year.
The next-generation cell phones, which are expected to be able to transfer pictures, will be available in the marketplace by the beginning of 2001, a KDD spokesman said.
